category.title: Binary Search & Monotonic Space
category.description: Binary search on arrays, answer spaces, and 2D matrices.

algorithms.title: Binary Search & Lower/Upper Bound Patterns
algorithms.summary: Divide-and-conquer technique to locate elements or decision thresholds in sorted arrays or monotonic search spaces.
explanation: Maintain search space range `[low, high]`.
Compute `mid = low + (high - low) // 2` to prevent integer overflow.
Check condition at `mid`:
- If `arr[mid] == target`, return `mid`.
- If `arr[mid] < target`, shrink search space to right `low = mid + 1`.
- If `arr[mid] > target`, shrink search space to left `high = mid - 1`.
For Binary Search on Answer Space: Replace array with boolean function `check(mid)` that is monotonic (TTT...FFF or FFF...TTT).

traceSteps: Returns index 3 in O(log N) iterations.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds an item or optimal threshold value in logarithmic O(log N) operations.
wAnswers.whenToUse: Whenever data is sorted, or whenever problem asks for min/max threshold matching a condition.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Database B-Tree indexing, Git bisect (finding bug commit), memory allocation address lookup, binary search trees.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Reduces search space by half in each iteration: O(log₂ N). 1 Billion elements searched in just 30 comparisons!

algorithms.title: Standard Binary Search, Lower Bound & Upper Bound
algorithms.summary: Foundational binary search techniques for searching sorted arrays and finding Lower Bound (first element ≥ target), Upper Bound (first element > target), and Search Insert Position.
explanation: Standard Binary Search: Search for exact match by checking mid = low + (high - low) // 2.
Lower Bound: Finds first index `i` where `arr[i] >= target`. If target > max, returns N.
Upper Bound: Finds first index `i` where `arr[i] > target`. Useful for range queries.
Search Insert Position: Equivalent to Lower Bound index where target should be inserted.

traceSteps: Lower Bound for 5: low=0, high=4. mid=2 (5 >= 5) -> high=2. mid=0 (1 < 5) -> low=1. mid=1 (3 < 5) -> low=2. Return index 2.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds target elements and exact boundary positions in logarithmic O(log N) time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When searching, inserting, or querying range boundaries in sorted data.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Database range queries, C++ std::lower_bound / std::upper_bound, Java Arrays.binarySearch.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Halves the search space at each iteration, reducing O(N) linear scan to O(log N).

algorithms.title: First & Last Occurrence & Count in Sorted Array
algorithms.summary: Finds the first and last index of a target value in a sorted array and computes total occurrence count (last - first + 1) in O(log N) time.
explanation: First Occurrence: Binary Search saving index when `arr[mid] == target`, then continuing search in left half (`high = mid - 1`).
Last Occurrence: Binary Search saving index when `arr[mid] == target`, then continuing search in right half (`low = mid + 1`).
Total Occurrence Count: If target exists, `count = last_occurrence - first_occurrence + 1`.
Avoids linear scanning when duplicate target values span a large portion of the array.

traceSteps: Search First Occurrence of 8: mid index 3 (val 8) -> save bound=3, move high to 2. First occurrence = index 3.
Search Last Occurrence of 8: mid index 3 (val 8) -> save bound=3, move low to 4. mid index 4 (val 8) -> save bound=4, move low to 5. Last occurrence = index 4.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Locates boundary range of repeated elements in O(log N) logarithmic time.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding first/last position or total count of duplicate items in sorted data.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Database index range scans, frequency counting in sorted logs.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Replaces O(N) duplicate scanning with two O(log N) binary searches.

algorithms.title: Rotated Sorted Array (Search, Minimum & Rotation Point)
algorithms.summary: Searches for a target, finds the minimum element, and determines rotation count in a rotated sorted array in O(log N) time.
explanation: Key Insight: In a rotated sorted array, AT LEAST ONE HALF (left or right) is ALWAYS strictly sorted!
Search Target: Check if `nums[low] <= nums[mid]` (Left half sorted). If target lies in left range `[nums[low], nums[mid]]`, search left; else search right.
If right half is sorted (`nums[mid] <= nums[high]`), check if target lies in `[nums[mid], nums[high]]`.
Find Minimum / Rotation Point: Minimum element is the pivot point where `nums[mid] > nums[high]`. Index of minimum = number of rotations.

traceSteps: low=0 (val 4), high=6 (val 2), mid=3 (val 7). Left half [4..7] is sorted.
Target 0 is not in range [4..7]. Search right half: low = 4.
low=4 (val 0), high=6 (val 2), mid=5 (val 1). Right half [0..2] is sorted.
mid index 4 has value 0 == target! Return index 4.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Searches and finds minimum elements in shifted/rotated sorted arrays.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When array was sorted then rotated by unknown offset K.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Circular buffer searching, time-series log offsets.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Identifies the sorted half at each step to maintain logarithmic O(log N) time.

algorithms.title: BS on Answer: Koko Eating Bananas & Ship Packages
algorithms.summary: Solves minimum capacity / speed problems by binary searching over monotonic answer range `[1...MaxVal]` with a feasibility helper function.
explanation: Pattern: When asked to find minimum capacity or rate K such that a task can be finished within D days / H hours.
Define Search Range: `low = 1` or `max(weights)`, `high = max(piles)` or `sum(weights)`.
Feasibility Helper `is_possible(k)`: Calculates total hours/days needed if eating speed / ship capacity is `k`.
If `is_possible(mid) <= H`: `mid` is valid! Try smaller speed `high = mid - 1`.
Else: Speed too slow, increase speed `low = mid + 1`.

traceSteps: mid = 6: Hours needed = 1+1+2+2 = 6 <= 8 (Valid!). Try smaller speed: high = 5.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds minimum valid threshold capacity or speed across monotonic search spaces.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When optimizing a rate/capacity constraint with monotonic binary feasibility (True/False transition).
wAnswers.whereUsed: Resource rate allocation, bandwidth throttling, deadline scheduling.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Replaces brute force rate checking with logarithmic range evaluation.

algorithms.title: BS on Answer: Aggressive Cows & Max-Min Distance
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(N log(MaxDist)) after sorting stalls in O(N log N)
algorithms.summary: Maximizes the minimum distance between C placed elements (e.g. cows in stalls or balls in buckets) using Binary Search on Answer.
explanation: Problem: Place C cows into N stalls such that the minimum distance between any two cows is as LARGE as possible.
Sort stall positions.
Define distance search range `low = 1` and `high = stalls[N-1] - stalls[0]`.
Feasibility Helper `can_place(dist)`: Greedily place first cow at stall 0. Place next cow at first stall with distance `>= dist`.
If `can_place(mid) >= C`: Distance `mid` is valid! Try larger distance `ans = mid`, `low = mid + 1`.
Else: Distance too large, decrease distance `high = mid - 1`.

traceSteps: Sorted stalls = [1, 2, 4, 8, 9]. Distance range: low = 1, high = 8.
mid = 4: Place cows at 1, 8. Total cows = 2 < 3 (Failed!). Try high = 3.
mid = 3: Place cows at 1, 4, 8. Total cows = 3 >= 3 (Valid!). Try low = 4.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Maximizes minimum separation distance among placed objects.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When finding maximum minimum distance in spatial placement problems.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Cellular tower placement, distance optimization in wireless networks.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Greedy feasibility check + Binary search on distance gives O(N log(Range)) efficiency.

algorithms.title: BS on Answer: Allocate Books & Split Array Sum
algorithms.summary: Minimizes the maximum subarray sum when allocating N contiguous items to M partitions (Book Allocation, Painter's Partition, Split Array Largest Sum).
explanation: Problem: Allocate N contiguous books to M students such that the maximum pages assigned to any student is MINIMIZED.
Range: `low = max(pages)` (at least largest single book), `high = sum(pages)` (one student gets all books).
Feasibility Helper `is_possible(max_pages)`: Iterate through books adding pages. If current student exceeds `max_pages`, allocate to a new student.
If required students `<= M`: Capacity `max_pages` is valid! Try smaller capacity `ans = mid`, `high = mid - 1`.
Else: Capacity too small, increase capacity `low = mid + 1`.

traceSteps: mid = 21: Partition 1 [7,2,5,10] sum=24 > 21 -> split: [7,2,5]=14, [10,8]=18. Students needed = 2 <= 2 (Valid!). Try high = 20.
mid = 18: Partition 1 [7,2,5]=14, Partition 2 [10,8]=18. Students needed = 2 <= 2 (Valid!). Try high = 17.
mid = 17: Partition 1 [7,2,5]=14, Partition 2 [10]=10, Partition 3 [8]=8. Students = 3 > 2 (Failed!). low = 18.

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Minimizes the maximum workload among M parallel partitions.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When partitioning contiguous items to M workers/subarrays to balance load.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Load balancers, CPU thread task partitioners, painter partitioning.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Binary search on max capacity guarantees global optimal balance in logarithmic steps.

algorithms.title: 2D Binary Search & Staircase Search Matrix
algorithms.timeComplexity: O(log(M*N)) for 1D mapped matrix, O(M + N) for Staircase search
algorithms.summary: Searches for a target value in 2D sorted matrices using index mapping virtual 1D binary search or top-right staircase elimination.
explanation: Pattern 1 (Fully Sorted 2D Matrix): Treat M x N matrix as a virtual 1D sorted array of length M*N.
Map 1D index `mid` to 2D matrix cell: `row = mid // N`, `col = mid % N`.
Perform standard binary search on `low = 0` to `high = M*N - 1` in O(log(M*N)) time.
Pattern 2 (Row-wise & Column-wise Sorted Matrix II): Start at Top-Right corner `row = 0, col = N - 1`.
If `matrix[row][col] == target`: Found!
If `matrix[row][col] > target`: Move Left (`col--`).
If `matrix[row][col] < target`: Move Down (`row++`). Time: O(M + N).

wAnswers.whatItSolves: Finds targets in 2D grid structures without scanning all cells.
wAnswers.whenToUse: When searching in sorted 2D matrices or grids.
wAnswers.whereUsed: Image pixel region lookup, GIS spatial grid queries, database 2D index lookup.
wAnswers.whyOptimal: Replaces O(M*N) grid scan with O(log(M*N)) or O(M+N) staircase search.

def searchMatrix(matrix: list[list[int]], target: int) -> bool:
    if not matrix or not matrix[0]: return False
    m, n = len(matrix), len(matrix[0])
    low, high = 0, m * n - 1
    
    while low <= high:
        mid = (low + high) // 2
        r, c = mid // n, mid % n
        val = matrix[r][c]
        if val == target: return True
        elif val < target: low = mid + 1
        else: high = mid - 1
    return False

def searchMatrixII(matrix: list[list[int]], target: int) -> bool:
    if not matrix or not matrix[0]: return False
    r, c = 0, len(matrix[0]) - 1
    while r < len(matrix) and c >= 0:
        val = matrix[r][c]
        if val == target: return True
        elif val > target: c -= 1
        else: r += 1
    return False
